sets.title: DeckCheck sweep 2026-10-18: eleven standouts for the meanest bracket-4 Edgar — exile-wipe answers, death-triggered draw, distance drain, input
sets.source: deckcheck.co Explore Cards (Synergetic 300 + Recommendations 200), read against the DTI 28/96 scan and roast
sets.query: DeckCheck builder qb9leISdSZX6 → Explore Cards → Synergetic Cards / Recommendations; 320 distinct cards, 0 in the deck, 70 cut in earlier versions

cards.name: Clever Concealment
cards.why: convoke (the tokens pay), your permanents phase out: beats Farewell and an overloaded Cyclonic Rift, which Boros Charm and Flawless Maneuver do not — the roast's one valid critical point

cards.name: Enduring Tenacity
cards.why: Sanguine Bond on a 4-mana lifelink body that returns as an enchantment when it dies: a seventh combo half with Exquisite Blood, and a destroy wipe leaves the drain on the table

cards.name: Enduring Innocence
cards.why: draws a card whenever small creatures enter, once a turn — eminence tokens enter every turn; comes back as an enchantment after a destroy wipe; lifelink body

cards.name: Morbid Opportunist
cards.why: 3 mana, draw when creatures die, once a turn: death-triggered draw, the pilot's preferred shape for the turn 7-8 empty hand

cards.name: Tocasia's Welcome
cards.why: enchantment: draw when creatures with mana value 3 or less enter, once a turn — tokens are mv 0; survives creature wipes

cards.name: Niv-Mizzet, Ghost Counsel
cards.why: whenever you gain life, pay that much life to draw that many cards — a mana-free draw engine in a drain deck, and a tap drain

cards.name: Vraan, Executioner Thane
cards.why: 2 mana, the first time creatures you control die each turn each opponent loses 2 and you gain 2: action at a distance on a cheap body

cards.name: Vein Ripper
cards.why: 6 mana flyer: any creature dying is 2 drained from an opponent; ward—sacrifice a creature makes removal cost a body; the biggest distance payoff on either tab

cards.name: Dictate of Erebos
cards.why: flash: every token death makes each opponent sacrifice a creature; lands after a wipe resolves and turns the rebuild into removal

cards.name: Urza's Incubator
cards.why: Vampire spells cost 2 less; eminence triggers on cast, so cheaper casts are more tokens per turn — the input thesis

cards.name: Bolas's Citadel
cards.why: play from the top paying life, which this deck makes back; the bracket-4 card-advantage engine on the Recommendations tab

sets.title: DeckCheck 'power tune' 2026-10-19: the five of eighteen adds never in an Edgar list, read through the input thesis. The other thirteen were the pilot's own earlier cuts (the August go-wide aristocrats list), and the cuts included Vish Kal and Sanguine Bond — passed, not watched.
sets.source: deckcheck.co Power Tune (5 credits), builder qb9leISdSZX6

cards.name: Talisman of Hierarchy
cards.why: two-mana rock that fixes W/B: input for the cast trigger, cheap and boring. Never in an Edgar list before.

cards.name: Talisman of Conviction
cards.why: two-mana rock that fixes R/W: the second rock the curve wants. Never in an Edgar list before.

cards.name: Phyrexian Tower
cards.why: a land that is also a sacrifice outlet and burst mana: input with no slot cost. Never tried.

cards.name: Clavileño, First of the Blessed
cards.why: death-triggered draw plus evasive Demon tokens: the draw axis the pilot requires on every Edgar change. Never tried.

cards.name: Bartolomé del Presidio
cards.why: a free repeatable sac outlet at two mana; only earns a slot if the combo build still sacrifices enough. Never tried.

sets.title: DeckCheck I2 Proactive Denial reads F (0 of 8): the deck runs no tax, lock, edict engine or resource strip. The pilot's rule for this set: only DUAL-PURPOSE denial — each card must also pay the profile (drain, tribe, pressure) — no symmetric stax (rule-of-law, Thalia, Strict Proctor, Torpor Orb effects tax Edgar's own spell-heavy plan). Three or four slots at most. The goldfish cannot see any of these, so net-change reads only what the pulled slots cost; the verdict is judgment, then DeckCheck's rescan, then games.
sets.source: the pilot's Atlas pile (Drana and Linvala, Kambal) + DeckCheck I2 roast + corpus card-search 2026-10-19
sets.query: proactive denial, dual-purpose, Mardu, Vampires first

cards.name: Drana and Linvala
cards.why: the lock: activated abilities of opponents' creatures can't be activated, and she has them all — a 3/4 flying vigilance Vampire Angel Edgar's eminence makes cheaper; the pilot's pick from the Atlas pile. Denial on a threat body.

cards.name: Charismatic Conqueror
cards.why: two-mana Vampire: an opponent's artifact or creature entering untapped either taps or hands you a 1/1 lifelink Vampire — a tax on rocks and dorks that is also token fuel for Vraan, Morbid Opportunist, Tenacity and the sac outlets. Was in v1.0.0, cut at the v2.0.0 Mardu-combo pivot (2026-10-05); the pilot wants it back in view.

cards.name: Anowon, the Ruin Sage
cards.why: at the beginning of your upkeep each opponent sacrifices a non-Vampire creature: an asymmetric edict engine that spares the tribe — the pilot's pick ('Anowon is great').

cards.name: Kambal, Consul of Allocation
cards.why: opponents lose 2 life per noncreature spell and you gain 2: a tax that is drain AND life gain, so every opposing spell triggers Sanguine Bond / Enduring Tenacity. The card that turns the denial metric into the combo. In the Atlas pile.

cards.name: Butcher of Malakir
cards.why: Grave Pact on a 5/4 flying Vampire: every death on your side is an edict for each opponent. Seven mana — the question is whether the deck reaches it.

cards.name: Dictate of Erebos
cards.why: the Grave Pact effect at flash speed, five mana. Was in the mean-v1 package as Elspeth's replacement and came out in option C for that reason only; as a denial piece in its own slot it is a separate question.
